intro: If you're someone who has to come work or handle business around the Amata City and Eastern Seaboard industrial estates on the Pluak Daeng side, and you want a clean room close to work at a price that won't spiral — Grand Esie Service Apartment is a name workers in this area know well · This is a 2-star serviced apartment in Map Yang Phon subdistrict, Pluak Daeng district, in a building with 78 rooms in total, every one with a balcony, AC, a fridge, and a TV · What a lot of people mention is the location less than 2 kilometers from the estates and the friendly service that scores as high as 9.4 · There's no swimming pool here and it's no luxury resort, but it leans on a simple strength: rooms that actually work, taking both daily and monthly stays, from about ฿500/night · Overall 8.2 out of 10 on Trip.com and 4.0 from 62 reviews on Google

body.html: Overview and who it suits — To put it as briefly as possible, Grand Esie Service Apartment is for people who want "a clean room near work for a few hundred baht" in the middle of the Pluak Daeng industrial area, rather than people hunting for a resort with a pool and full facilities · It's a 2-star serviced apartment that has been open since 2007 and was renovated around 2013, located in Map Yang Phon subdistrict, Pluak Daeng district — an area surrounded by large industrial estates such as Amata City, Eastern Seaboard, and Siam Eastern · The building has 78 rooms in total and takes both nightly guests and long-stay monthly guests, so the overall vibe is more of a workers' residence mixed with traveler lodging than a tourist hotel · Voices from real reviews line up on who fits here: staff and engineers coming to work at the estates on a permanent or temporary basis, technicians and project teams who need to stay in the area for several weeks, drivers or people visiting factories, and budget travelers passing through the eastern route who just need an overnight stay near the estates · On the flip side, anyone after a seaside getaway, a resort with a pool, or a location near attractions like Pattaya and Bang Saen may find this isn't the answer, because the property sits deep inside the industrial zone, a fair distance from the sea · Put simply, Grand Esie sells the convenience of getting in and out of the estates, value for money, and friendly service more than views or luxury — which is why its service score climbs as high as 9.4 while the price stays at a level workers can afford every month

Location and getting around — This is the heart of Grand Esie and the reason people choose to stay here · The property sits at 284 Moo 4, Map Yang Phon subdistrict, Pluak Daeng district, in the middle of the eastern industrial zone · The upside of this location is that it's close to several major industrial estates within a short drive — Amata City (formerly Amata City Rayong) and the Eastern Seaboard are about 1.9-2 kilometers away, Siam Eastern estate is nearby, and many factories in this area are within a 5-15 min drive · Around the property there's ESIE Plaza, the estate area's shops-and-restaurants hub, about 1.5 kilometers away, Sapan 4 Market about 3.9 kilometers away, and several 7-Eleven convenience stores scattered around the property, which many reviewers say makes buying food and daily items easy · For longer trips, it's about 50-58 kilometers from U-Tapao Airport (UTP), or roughly a 50-55 min drive, and about 30 kilometers from Pattaya · The honest note to make about this location is that the Pluak Daeng-Map Yang Phon area is an industrial zone where public transport is limited — the streets around the property are factory roads rather than walkways, so if you need to get in and out of the estates or go beyond the immediate area, having your own car or motorbike is the most convenient option, which the property supports with free parking, and it sits where many factories' employee shuttles pass by

"Stayed several months while working near the estates. The room was clean, the staff were lovely and really helpful, you can park right in front of your room, it's close to work and a 7-Eleven, and the price isn't expensive. Good value if you're here for work."

Room types and decor — Grand Esie is a mid-sized building with 78 rooms in total, split into several types by size and view · The main options are the Deluxe Twin (Old Port View), a twin-bed room looking out toward the exterior, good for colleagues or couples, and the Standard Interior View Room, a single-bed room facing the inside of the building, cheaper for solo guests · The decor is the simple style of a workers' serviced apartment, leaning on being functional rather than pretty · A good point is that every room has a private balcony, which helps with ventilation and drying laundry for long-stay guests, and every room has AC, a fridge, an LCD TV, an en-suite bathroom with a water heater, and a decent amount of storage space · Most real reviews praise the rooms as clean, free of musty smells, more spacious than expected at this price, and with reasonably comfortable beds — many long-stay guests say they're comfortable enough to work in all week · But to be straight, there are notes worth knowing — some reviews say some of the fixtures and furniture are starting to show their age, in line with a building open since 2007 and last renovated around 2013, so there are signs of wear in places · On top of that, room quality and views vary by type, so if you want a brighter room, choose the Twin facing outward over the Interior facing inward, and state your preference when you book

Facilities and the pool — It has to be said up front that Grand Esie has no swimming pool, a limitation worth knowing before you book, because it positions itself as a budget workers' serviced apartment, not a tourist resort · The facilities it does have are tuned to match a work stay — there's free Wi-Fi in the common areas, free parking in the building with easy spots right in front of your room, a 24-hour front desk that helps workers coming and going on late shifts, a spa and massage room to unwind after work, luggage storage, and laundry service, which long-stay monthly guests use often · There's also a shared kitchen in the building for guests to cook or reheat food, plus a picnic area and barbecue (BBQ) grill that lets groups of colleagues cook together on weekends · The real selling point here isn't a long list of luxury facilities but the ease of getting in and out of the estates and the basic, functional things that work for someone who's here for work · For people who come specifically to work in the industrial area, this is a set of facilities that fits day-to-day life · But for anyone who wants a pool, a full gym, or leisure activities on-site, you have to accept this place can't deliver that, and you should look for a higher-budget resort or the Pattaya side instead

Food and places to eat nearby — Grand Esie offers a local-style breakfast from 6:00 AM-10:00 AM, charged separately from the room rate, which is handy for people rushing to an early shift · But what keeps food from being a problem is the location right in the middle of the estate area, which has plenty of restaurants and convenience stores serving workers · Near the property there's ESIE Plaza, which gathers the estate area's restaurants, cafes, and shops within a short drive, and Sapan 4 Market selling local food at everyday prices · Around the property there are also made-to-order eateries, curry-over-rice shops, and noodle shops open for factory staff, plus several 7-Eleven branches that reviewers say are a short walk or drive away · For long-stay guests who want to save, the shared kitchen in the building helps a lot, especially for people who buy ingredients at the market to cook themselves, or use the BBQ area for a weekend grill with colleagues · The advantage of this area is that food comes in worker-priced options, so you don't have to rely on the property's food for every meal · Overall, food at Grand Esie isn't the reason to come for eating on-site, but it's a location that gives you easy access to the estate area's restaurants and food, which most workers see as enough for daily life

Service and staff — Service is the most praised aspect and the highest-scoring side in real reviews, at 9.4 out of 10 · Many agree the staff are friendly, helpful, attentive like people you know, and flexible about late-shift workers coming and going thanks to the 24-hour front desk · For people on long monthly stays, friendly service and conversations that understand the estate-worker lifestyle are a big reason many choose to stay on and come back · There's luggage storage, laundry, and help coordinating various things in an area with limited public transport, which makes daily life more convenient · But for balance, it has to be said honestly that the number of reviews on an international platform like Trip.com is still small (around 3 reviews), while Google has 62 reviews at an overall score of about 4.0 out of 5, which reflects an overall reception that's good but not perfect, with some voices noting that the facilities are fairly basic and the building is starting to age · On the whole, service remains the clearest strength here, and it's one reason the overall review score sits at a satisfying level for accommodation at this price

Voices from real reviews (praise and gripes) — Pulled together from Trip.com, Google, and other booking sources, the picture is fairly consistent · On the praise side: friendly, helpful service and staff (the highest-scoring side at 9.4), a location near Amata City and the Eastern Seaboard that makes getting to and from work easy, clean rooms with no musty smell, parking that's convenient right in front of the room, being close to 7-Eleven convenience stores and the estate area's restaurants, budget prices suited to long monthly stays, and a balcony in every room that helps with ventilation and drying laundry · On the gripes side: what comes up is no swimming pool and fairly basic facilities, some fixtures and parts of the building starting to age in line with being open since 2007 and last renovated around 2013, a location deep in the industrial zone so it's far from shopping and the sea and you have to drive out, and breakfast being charged separately from the room rate · Most of these gripes are matters of setting your expectations correctly for budget workers' accommodation and being fine with it, rather than big problems, because the overall score still sits at 8.2 on Trip.com and many people here for work say it's worth it and stay on for months

"The room was more spacious than I expected and clean, with a balcony for drying laundry, and it's near the estates so it's only a few minutes' drive to work · The one gripe is that some things are starting to age, and there's no pool, but at this price for a work stay it's really okay."

Price comparison and value — Nightly room rates start at about ฿500/night for a Standard Interior room on a weekday and climb to around ฿700-฿1,100 for a Deluxe Twin or during busy periods at the estates, with some international platforms showing prices in roughly the 15-32 US dollar range · What makes Grand Esie genuinely good value is the monthly rate designed specifically for estate workers, which works out much cheaper per night than booking nightly and is why many choose to stay long-term as a work base · Compared with the same kind of accommodation in the Sriracha-Laem Chabang industrial area, like serviced apartments where prices climb into the mid-thousands to two thousand, or a chain hotel like Kameo Amata Bangpakong that costs more and has fuller facilities, Grand Esie clearly wins on price and on being close to the Pluak Daeng-side estates, but loses on the pool, how new the building is, and tourist facilities · In short, if you weight a tight budget, being close to Amata City, and a long stay for work, every baht you spend comes back as good value, especially for people who have to be in the area for several weeks to several months

What to know before you book — There are several things that help make a stay smoother · One, there's no swimming pool here and the facilities are fairly basic, so if you want a pool or a leisure vibe, consider a resort-type property on the Pattaya side · Two, if you care about a bright room, choose the Deluxe Twin facing outward over the Interior facing inward, and specify it when you book · Three, if you plan to stay long to work at the estates, you should contact the property directly to ask about the monthly rate, which is usually much cheaper than booking nightly through a platform · Four, breakfast is charged separately from the room rate, so if you don't want it you can eat at the shops around the estates · Five, the Pluak Daeng-Map Yang Phon area has limited public transport, so if you don't have your own car you should plan ahead — motorbike taxi, a factory's employee shuttle, or a ride-hailing service — and the property has free parking for those who drive themselves · Six, since the property is in the industrial zone with factory roads all around, set your expectations that the surroundings are a work area, not a tourist district · Seven, read the cancellation and refund terms carefully before paying, and choose free cancellation if your plans aren't firm yet

Verdict — From all the real reviews, Grand Esie Service Apartment is the best fit for people who have to come work or handle business at the Pluak Daeng-Map Yang Phon industrial estates and want a clean room close to work on a budget, for both daily and monthly stays · Service scoring as high as 9.4, being close to Amata City and the Eastern Seaboard, clean rooms with a balcony in every one, a shared kitchen, and a BBQ area make it good value for staff, engineers, technicians, and budget travelers who have to be in the area · But you do have to accept that there's no swimming pool, the facilities are fairly basic, the building and some fixtures are starting to age in line with being open since 2007, and the location sits deep in the industrial zone, far from the sea and shopping · If you're looking for a resort with a pool, a seaside getaway vibe, or a location near attractions, this may not be the answer, and you should look at options on the Pattaya or Bang Saen side instead · But for a budget-friendly work stay near the estates, where you want ease of getting in and out of work and friendly service — Grand Esie meets that need well, and it's the reason workers in this area choose to stay on for months at a time

honestChecks: If you're here on a leisure trip and want a resort with a seaside pool — this is a workers' serviced apartment in the estate zone, with no pool and a fair distance from the sea → if relaxation is the priority, look at options on the Pattaya side like Centara Grand Mirage or the Bang Saen side

If you want a brand-new room and full facilities — the building opened in 2007 and was last renovated around 2013, so some spots are starting to age → set your expectations on value and being close to the estates, or ask to see a room in good condition when you book

If you don't have your own car — the Pluak Daeng-Map Yang Phon area has limited public transport and factory roads all around → plan ahead for a motorbike taxi, an employee shuttle, or ride-hailing, and use the free parking if you drive yourself

faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions — Grand Esie Service Apartment

faq.q: Where is Grand Esie Service Apartment · which estates is it near?
faq.a: The property sits at 284 Moo 4, Map Yang Phon subdistrict, Pluak Daeng district, in the heart of the eastern industrial estate area · It's close to the Amata City and Eastern Seaboard estates, about 1.9-2 kilometers away, and near the Siam Eastern estate · ESIE Plaza is about 1.5 km away and Sapan 4 Market about 3.9 km · It's about 30 km from Pattaya and about 50-58 km from U-Tapao Airport.

faq.q: Does Grand Esie have a swimming pool and breakfast?
faq.a: No swimming pool, since it's a budget workers' serviced apartment · There's a local-style breakfast served 6:00 AM-10:00 AM, charged separately from the room rate · There's a shared kitchen in the building, plus a picnic area and BBQ grill for cooking yourself · If you want a pool and a leisure vibe, look at resort-type accommodation on the Pattaya or Bang Saen side.

faq.q: What's the starting price at Grand Esie · can you stay monthly?
faq.a: Prices start at about ฿500/night for a Standard Interior room on a weekday, climbing to around ฿700-฿1,100 for a Deluxe Twin · The highlight is the monthly rate for estate workers, which works out much cheaper per night than nightly · We recommend contacting the property directly (call 090-974-8598) to ask about the monthly rate and availability.

faq.q: Who does Grand Esie suit best?
faq.a: It's a great fit for staff, engineers, technicians, and people coming to work or handle business at the Pluak Daeng-Map Yang Phon industrial estates who want a clean room close to work on a budget, for both daily and monthly stays · As well as budget travelers passing through the eastern route · It's not a fit for people on a leisure trip who want a resort with a pool or a seaside location, who should look at the Pattaya or Bang Saen side instead.

faq.q: What are the rooms and service like at Grand Esie?
faq.a: The building has 78 rooms, each with a balcony, AC, a fridge, and a TV · Most reviews praise the rooms as clean with no musty smell and more spacious than expected at this price · The highest-scoring side is service at 9.4 — staff are friendly and helpful, with a 24-hour front desk · The note is that some fixtures and parts of the building are starting to age in line with being open since 2007; if you want a brighter room, choose the Twin facing outward.

faq.q: Is it convenient to get to Grand Esie without a car?
faq.a: The Pluak Daeng-Map Yang Phon area is an industrial zone where public transport is limited and the streets around are factory roads · If you don't have your own car, plan ahead — a motorbike taxi, a factory's employee shuttle, or a ride-hailing service · The property has free parking in front of the room for those who drive themselves, which is the most convenient way to get in and out of the estates and reach shopping around the area.
